title: Legislative districts of Leyte

{{Short description|Philippine electoral districts}} {{Use mdy dates|date=November 2022}} {{Use Philippine English|date=November 2022}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Leyte''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Leyte (province)|Leyte]], the [[Cities of the Philippines#Independent cities|independent component city]] of [[Ormoc]], and [[Cities of the Philippines#Independent cities|highly urbanized city]] of [[Tacloban]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province, together with the independent cities are currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through their [[Leyte's 1st congressional district|first]], [[Leyte's 2nd congressional district|second]], [[Leyte's 3rd congressional district|third]], [[Leyte's 4th congressional district|fourth]], and [[Leyte's 5th congressional district|fifth]] congressional districts. [[Southern Leyte]] and [[Biliran]] last formed part of the province's representation in 1961 and 1995, respectively. == History == Leyte was originally divided into four [[House of Representatives of the Philippines#District representation|congressional districts]] from 1907 until 1931, when it was redistricted to five [[House of Representatives of the Philippines#District representation|congressional districts]] by virtue of Act No. 3788.{{cite web |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xuIxAQAAIAAJ |title=Public laws enacted by the Philippine Legislature: during the period from Sept. 1, 1900 to Nov. 14, 1935; comprising acts nos. 1 to 4275, Volume 31 |author=Philippine Legislature |date=1935 |access-date=August 1, 2019}} When seats for the [[Senate of the Philippines|upper house]] of the [[Philippine Legislature]] were elected from territory-based districts between 1916 and 1935, the province formed part of the [[Senatorial districts of the Philippines#Ninth District|ninth senatorial district]] which elected two out of the 24-member senate. In the disruption caused by the [[Second World War]], [[#1943–1944|two delegates]] represented the province in the [[National Assembly of the Second Philippine Republic|National Assembly]] of the Japanese-sponsored [[Second Philippine Republic]]: one was the provincial governor (an [[ex officio member|''ex officio'' member]]), while the other was elected through a provincial assembly of [[KALIBAPI]] members during the [[Japanese occupation of the Philippines]]. Upon the restoration of the [[Philippine Commonwealth]] in 1945, the province retained its five pre-war representative districts. Even after receiving their own city charters, [[Ormoc]] and [[Tacloban]] remained part of the representation of the Province of Leyte by virtue of Section 90 of Republic Act No. 179 (June 21, 1947),{{cite web|url=http://www.chanrobles.com/republicacts/republicactno179.html|date=June 21, 1947|author=Congress of the Philippines|website=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library|access-date=August 1, 2019|title=Republic Act No. 179 – An Act Creating Ormoc City|archive-date=May 29, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180529203746/http://www.chanrobles.com/republicacts/republicactno179.html|url-status=live}} and Section 91 of Republic Act No. 760 (June 20, 1952),{{cite web|url=http://www.chanrobles.com/republicacts/republicactno760.html|date=June 20, 1952|author=Congress of the Philippines|website=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library|access-date=August 1, 2019|title=Republic Act No. 760 – An Act Creating the City of Tacloban|archive-date=December 25, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181225062536/http://www.chanrobles.com/republicacts/republicactno760.html|url-status=live}} respectively. Republic Act No. 2227, enacted on May 22, 1959, created the province of [[Southern Leyte]] from the southern municipalities of Leyte that constituted its [[#1931–1961_3|third congressional district]].{{cite web|title=Republic Act No. 2227 - An Act Creating the Province of Southern Leyte|url=http://www.lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1959/ra_2227_1959.html|website=The LawPhil Project|access-date=August 1, 2019|date=May 22, 1959|archive-date=August 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190801140217/https://www.lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1959/ra_2227_1959.html|url-status=live}} Per Section 5 of R.A. 2227, the incumbent representatives of all five districts of Leyte continued to serve for the remainder of [[4th Congress of the Philippines|4th Congress]]. Starting in the [[1961 Philippine House of Representatives elections|1961 elections]], Leyte's remaining four districts were renumbered; the [[#1931–1961|first]], [[#1931–1961_2|second]], [[#1931–1961_4|fourth]] and [[#1931–1961_5|fifth]] districts were re-designated as the [[#1961–1972_3|third]], [[#1961–1972_4|fourth]], [[#1961–1972|first]] and [[#1961–1972_2|second]] districts, respectively. Leyte was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region VIII]] from 1978 to 1984. The province returned [[#1984–1986|five representatives, elected at-large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. Under the new Constitution which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, the province was re-apportioned into five districts,{{cite web |title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance |website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines |url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/ |author=1986 Constitutional Commission |date=February 2, 1987 |access-date=November 19, 2017 |archive-date=October 20, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171020013702/http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/ |url-status=live }} each of which elected its member to the restored [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. A plebiscite held on May 11, 1992, approved the establishment of Biliran (a sub-province of Leyte since 1959{{cite web |title=Republic Act No. 2141 - An Act Creating the Sub-Province of Biliran |url=http://www.chanrobles.com/republicacts/republicactno2141.html|website=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library |access-date=July 9, 2018}}) as a regular province, by virtue of Section 462 of Republic Act No. 7160 (Local Government Code of 1991).{{cite web|url=http://www.lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1991/ra_7160_1991.html|title=Republic Act No. 7160 - Local Government Code of 1991|access-date=August 1, 2019|date=October 10, 1991|author=Congress of the Philippines|archive-date=May 3, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160503071511/http://www.lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1991/ra_7160_1991.html|url-status=live}} Biliran continued to be represented as part of the [[#1987–1995|third district of Leyte]] until it elected its [[Legislative district of Biliran|own representative]] in the [[1995 Philippine general election|1995 elections]]. == Current districts == The province's current congressional delegation composes of two members of the [[Lakas–CMD]], one member of the [[Nationalist People's Coalition]], one member of the [[National Unity Party (Philippines)|National Unity Party]] and one member of the [[Partido Federal ng Pilipinas]]. {| class="wikitable sortable" style="margin: 1em auto; font-size:100%; line-height:20px; text-align:center" |+Legislative districts and representatives of [[Leyte (province)|Leyte]] ! rowspan="2" |District ! colspan="3" |Current Representative ! rowspan="2" |Party ! rowspan="2" |Constituent [[Local government in the Philippines|LGUs]] ! rowspan="2" |Population (2020){{cite web |url=https://psa.gov.ph/sites/default/files/attachments/ird/specialrelease/2_Table%201%20Population%20of%20Legislative%20Districts%20by%20Province%20and%20Selected%20HUC_Component%20City%20Web%20Final-signed.pdf |title=TABLE 1.
